advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'git could not run' (fail loud or at least log) from 'repo has no commits' in referencing_commits(), so caused_by_refusal only allows the link on a confirmed commit-less repo rather than on any non-zero git exit.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:56 `if found is None or found:` -> `return None` (None allows the link)

Docstring claims None means 'the history could not be read at all (not a repo, no commits yet)', but a non-zero returncode also fires on git-not-installed, corrupt object store, or a killed subprocess — worlds in which the check never actually ran yet the link is allowed.
advisory.finding: referencing_commits() returns None on ANY non-zero git exit (git binary missing, corrupt repo, permission error, interrupted process), and caused_by_refusal() treats None as 'allow the link'. A transient/environmental git failure is therefore indistinguishable from the intended 'no history yet' case and silently bypasses the caused_by guard — the check cannot tell 'checked and target has a commit' from 'the scan never ran'.
scenarios: CI/agent environment where git is unavailable or the repo is shallow/corrupt: every caused_by link is accepted unchecked, re-corrupting the escaped-defect lenses the guard exists to protect.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm extract_force's bare-`--force` following-token rule does not swallow a link positional when `--force` precedes the ids, or restrict the following-token capture so link's positional grammar is preserved.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:93-96 `nxt = argv[i + 1] ...` / `if nxt and not nxt.startswith("--"): reason = nxt; i += 1`

The following-token rule was safe for claim because claim's positionals precede/differ, but link has three positionals and the docstring claims one shared implementation for both; a leading bare `--force` mis-parses link's first positional as the reason.
advisory.finding: extract_force()'s bare `--force` following-token rule can consume a positional argument when `--force` precedes the positionals in `rebar link`. For `rebar link --force <bug> <target> caused_by`, `<bug>` (which does not start with `--`) is captured as the force reason, leaving rest=[<target>, caused_by] (len 2) and producing a spurious 'Usage' error instead of a forced link.
scenarios: A user or script invokes `rebar link --force <bug> <target> caused_by`: the intended forced link fails with a usage error and the reason is silently mis-captured.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for the `link` CLI write path with `--force` (inline and following-token spellings, including force placed before the relation positional) to pin extract_force's interaction with link's trailing positionals.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:74 `extract_force` — bare `--force` "consumes the NEXT token as its reason when that token does not start with `--`"
src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:213-217 `force, rest = extract_force([a for a in argv if a != "--dry-run"])` then `if len(rest) < 3: ... return 1`

tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py only drives link_cli in --dry-run form (lines 140, 158) with inline `--force=scope`; no non-dry-run link_cli force test and no `--force <token>` following-token case exists (search_files for extract_force / link_cli shows only these two call sites in tests)
advisory.finding: The newly-added shared extract_force following-token rule is applied to the `link` CLI (which has trailing positional args) with no test for the ordering hazard: `rebar link <bug> <target> --force caused_by` consumes `caused_by` as the --force reason (nxt does not start with `--`), leaving rest=[bug, target] which fails the `len(rest) < 3` positional-count check and prints the usage error instead of forcing the link. No test exercises the `link` CLI write path with --force in any position, so this regression is undetectable.
scenarios: A user runs `rebar link <bug> <target> --force caused_by` (force placed before the relation positional) and gets a usage error instead of a forced link, with no regression test to catch it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the caused_by edge presence (force-bypass row) and absence (commitless-target row) on the target's deps in the write-parity oracle, not just the subject's unchanged status.
evidence: tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py:79-84 ACCEPTED effect check reads `rebar.show_ticket(subject)['status']`; :89-94 REJECTED invariance check reads the same status — neither inspects deps/edges
tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py:280-284 link op links `tid -> target caused_by`; a link does not mutate `tid`'s status, so the status assertions are trivially satisfied for these rows
advisory.finding: The new op="link" write-parity rows do not verify the observable edge effect. For op="link" the oracle's ACCEPTED effect check asserts the SUBJECT's status (expected_status="open") and the REJECTED store-invariance check asserts unmutated_status="open", but a caused_by link never changes the subject ticket's status, so both assertions pass regardless of whether the caused_by edge was actually written (for the force-bypass row) or actually absent (for the commitless-target row). The parity rows verify cross-surface classification but are blind to a regression where an ACCEPTED link writes no edge or a REJECTED link leaks one.
scenarios: A surface classifies the force-bypass link ACCEPTED but silently writes no caused_by edge — the oracle still passes because the subject status is unchanged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the caused_by referencing-commit narrowing is an intended behavioral break and that all in-repo caused_by consumers (test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py:61, test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py) still pass under the None-history exemption.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:110 `if not force and (reason := caused_by_refusal(relation, tgt_id, str(tracker), _code_root(repo_root))):` raises CommandError for previously-accepted caused_by links

Pre-existing unforced caused_by consumers: tests/unit/test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py:61 `rebar.link(bug, origin, "caused_by", repo_root=repo)`, tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py:76/91/126 `rebar.link(bug, child/epic/stranger, "caused_by", ...)`

Mitigation confirmed: commitless repos exempted — src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py returns None when `proc.returncode != 0`, and caused_by_refusal returns None on `found is None`; the unit fixtures (test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py:33, test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py:48) git-init WITHOUT commits so those existing links stay allowed

Documented migration path with force= — docs/ticket-model.md notes `--force[=<reason>]` is the escape hatch; the diff updated interfaces tests that DO have history (test_caused_by_relation.py adds a commit, test_caused_by_relation_heldout.py adds force=)
advisory.finding: `rebar.link(..., "caused_by")` now narrows previously-valid input: a caused_by link is refused when the target has no referencing commit, changing runtime behavior for existing unforced consumers (a wire/behavioral backward-compat narrowing, mitigated by the documented force= escape hatch and the None-history exemption).
